transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I really appreciate it. 

I, um... I hope I'm explaining this the right way, but I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I just can’t seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. It's a bit embarrassing to admit at my age, and it's probably something I should be able to just handle, but... it's gotten a bit overwhelming lately. 

Between my regular work and side projects, there's just a lot—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions... and instead of prioritizing properly like a normal person, I just kind of... I end up starting whatever is loudest, you know? Whatever is right in front of my face, instead of what actually matters. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you help people with here.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Oh, um... I wouldn't say I'm bouncing off the walls or anything. I really try to be professional and sit still. But, well, I guess if I'm being completely honest... on those really long design calls for work, I do sometimes get this... I don't know, this sort of pressure building up in my body? Like I just physically need to stand up. 

So I might end up pacing around my home office a bit, or just kind of shifting from chair to chair. I always try to make sure I still look completely focused on the webcam, though! I really don't want my team to think I'm ignoring them or not taking the work seriously. 

Is that... does that count as what you're asking about? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

No, I don't think so. I really try to be thoughtful about my decisions, especially at work. I mean, I know how important it is to be reliable and steady, so I always try to think things through before I act. 

I guess... well, I might occasionally buy a new tool or software plug-in on a whim if I think it'll help with a project, but I don't think I do anything really impulsive or reckless. I'm definitely not the type to just jump into things without looking. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I try very hard to be responsible.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?

Well, I really do try my best to stay completely focused. My job requires a lot of concentration, and I want to make sure I'm doing good work. But... um, I guess if I'm being totally open about it, I do get a little sidetracked sometimes. 

It's usually just small things. Like, if I'm in the middle of coding and a Slack ping goes off, or one of my browser tabs flashes... or sometimes even if just a new visual idea pops into my head out of nowhere. I don't mean to, but I can sort of lose the thread of the code I was writing. I'll tell myself I'm just going to look at it for a second, and then maybe twenty minutes will go by because I ended up following some completely unrelated design rabbit hole. 

I always make sure to catch up and get my work done, though! I promise I don't just sit there ignoring my responsibilities. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee... I think everyone gets a little distracted by notifications these days, right? Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
Do you often have mood swings or find it hard to manage your emotions?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I really pride myself on being pretty even-keeled, especially at my age. You kind of have to be, right? Working in software, things break all the time, and you just have to stay calm and fix them. 

I mean, sure, I might get a little frustrated if a project is dragging on or if I've been stuck on a bug for hours, but I don't fly off the handle or anything like that. I always try to keep things professional and polite. I definitely wouldn't call them mood swings. Just... normal reactions to stress, I think? 

I hope that's what you mean. I try really hard not to let things get to me, and I think I do a pretty good job of keeping it all under control. Does that sound normal to you?
Do you often have trouble completing tasks or projects once you've started them?

Um, I wouldn't say I have trouble, no. I really make it a point to finish what I start. In my line of work, you kind of have to deliver, so I always make sure I get my projects done and hit my deadlines. 

I mean, I guess... well, maybe sometimes a personal side project or a hobby might sit around for a bit if I get really busy, but that's just because I'm prioritizing my actual job, you know? I really try to be dependable and see things through to the end. 

I hope that makes sense? I think it's pretty normal to have a few unfinished hobbies in your downtime if you're working full-time, right? I definitely wouldn't say it's a problem.
Do you often have difficulty keeping your workspace or living space organized?

Well, I really do try to keep things tidy. I mean, my desk at work isn't a total disaster zone or anything, and I always make sure the common areas at home are presentable. I don't want anyone thinking I'm a slob, you know? 

But... um, I guess if I'm being completely honest, things have been feeling a little overwhelming lately. It's actually kind of what finally pushed me to come in and talk to you. It's not so much the physical space, but... organizing all the moving parts in my life right now. 

I've got all these different things going on—like notes for a patent I'm working on, prep for a workshop, some gallery deadlines for my wife, and just trying to keep track of team decisions at work. I try to keep it all sorted, I really do, but lately, I just can't seem to manage it. I end up just starting on whatever is the loudest or most urgent thing in front of me, instead of what actually matters or what I had planned to do. 

I feel terrible about it because I really want to be on top of everything. I'm usually better at juggling things, I promise. It's just been a lot all at once. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm completely falling apart... I think everyone gets a little overwhelmed when they have too much on their plate, right?
Do you often struggle to follow through on instructions or fail to finish tasks due to distractions or lack of focus?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try to be the guy people can count on. If someone gives me instructions—like a project brief or a ticket at work—I make absolutely sure I follow through. I'd hate for anyone to think I wasn't paying attention or that I'm unreliable, you know? 

Um... sure, maybe I get a little distracted by an email popping up or someone asking a quick question, but I always get back on track and finish what I was asked to do. I mean, you kind of have to in my field, right? Otherwise, you wouldn't last very long. I really do my best to stay focused on what people need from me. 

So, no, I don't think I fail to finish things because of a lack of focus. I hope I'm understanding your question right? I just always want to make sure I'm doing exactly what's expected of me.
Do you often find your mind wandering away from the task you're trying to complete?

Well, I think everyone's mind wanders a little bit, right? Especially when you're staring at a screen all day. I really try to stay locked in on my code, I do. I want to make sure I'm writing clean, efficient stuff for the team. 

But, um... I guess sometimes it can be a little tricky. Like, if Slack pings, or if a browser tab flashes with a notification... I might glance at it just to make sure it's not urgent. I don't want to leave anyone hanging if they need me. 

And then... well, sometimes just a visual idea will pop into my head, maybe something related to my wife's gallery stuff or a different way to design a feature, and... I guess I can kind of lose the thread of what I was originally coding. Before I know it, I might spend, like, twenty minutes following some completely unrelated design rabbit hole. 

I always catch myself, though! And I get right back to work. I just... I have a lot of creative energy, I suppose, and sometimes it just spills over a bit. That's pretty normal for developers, don't you think? Just a little occupational hazard? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm not dedicated to my work.
Do you find it hard to concentrate on a single task for a long period of time?

Well, actually, no, I don't think so. I feel like I'm pretty good at that, to be honest. When I really need to sit down and build out a complex feature for work, I can stay at my desk for hours just focusing on that one main project. 

I mean, I really pride myself on being able to put my head down and grind through the tough stuff when the team needs me to. Even if, you know, like I mentioned before, I might glance at a Slack notification for a second, I'm still spending the whole afternoon working on that single task. I really want to make sure I'm giving my job the dedication it deserves, you know? 

So... no, sitting with one thing for a long time isn't really a problem for me. I hope that's a good sign? It means I'm still doing okay in that department, right?
Do you often find yourself struggling to maintain focus on a task from start to finish?

I mean, not really? I feel like I'm pretty good at seeing things through. Like I said, I can sit at my desk for hours working on a project, so I definitely get from the start to the finish eventually. 

I guess... well, sure, the path from start to finish might have a few little detours, like those design rabbit holes I mentioned, but I always get there. I really make sure the work gets done, and done well. I wouldn't want anyone thinking I leave things half-finished. 

I think as long as the end result is good and the team is happy, that's what really matters, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job. Is it normal to take a few little breaks or detours along the way, as long as you finish the task?
Do you often find yourself making careless mistakes in your work or other activities?

Oh, um... "careless" feels like a slightly harsh word, just because I really do care so much about the quality of my work. I'd hate for you or my team to think I'm just throwing things together without paying attention. 

But... well, I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, there are times during code reviews where I'll miss something... kind of embarrassingly small. Like, um, a reversed condition, or maybe just a version number in a dependency file. And then later, when someone points it out, I can see it was right in front of me the whole time, but I just sort of... skimmed past it, I guess? 

I always fix it right away, though! And I think when you're looking at hundreds of lines of complex logic, it's pretty normal for your eyes to just glaze over a tiny detail here and there, right? I mean, that's exactly why we do peer reviews in the first place, isn't it? To catch those little human errors? I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent.
Do you often feel like you're constantly 'on the go' or like you can't slow down?

Oh, no, definitely not. I think I'm actually a pretty calm guy. I mean, sitting at a computer all day for work, you kind of have to be able to just stay put, right? 

I definitely don't feel restless or like I'm constantly needing to be moving around. I like to think of myself as fairly grounded and easy-going. I really hope I come across that way to you, too? I'd hate to give off an erratic or hyper vibe. 

But yeah, no, I don't really struggle with slowing down at all. When work is done, I'm perfectly happy to just sit and relax. I assume it's a good sign that I'm able to just be still and take it easy like that?
Do you have trouble managing your emotional responses to stressful situations?

No, I wouldn't say so. I think I handle stress pretty well, actually. I mean, software development can be a high-pressure environment, especially when deadlines are tight or there's a critical bug, but I always try to stay professional and keep a level head. I really value being someone my team can rely on, you know? 

I guess... well, sometimes if I'm really overwhelmed and someone interrupts me when I'm deep in the middle of trying to fix a complex issue, I might get a tiny bit... brief with them? Just because I'm trying so hard to hold all the pieces of the problem in my head at once. But I always apologize right away if I think I sounded even a little bit sharp. I would never want to be difficult to work with or make anyone feel bad. 

I think everyone gets a little stressed when they're under the gun, right? As long as you don't take it out on people and you keep it professional, that's what counts. I try really hard to be easy to get along with, even when things are hectic. Does that sound like a normal way to handle work stress?
Do you often find yourself lacking motivation to start tasks?

Um, no, I don't think so. I actually really care about my work, so I'm usually pretty eager to get going. I would absolutely hate for my manager or anyone on the team to think I was... lazy, or dragging my feet, you know? 

I mean, occasionally I might spend a little extra time right at the beginning of a new project just... organizing my thoughts or getting my workspace set up perfectly before I actually start typing. But that's really just because I want to make sure I'm doing a good job right from the start. That's a good trait to have, right? Being thorough before you just blindly jump into something? 

But as far as lacking the actual drive to do the work, no, definitely not. I really pride myself on being dedicated and ready to contribute. I hope that comes across?
Do you often have difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or activities?

Um, no, not really. I think my attention span is actually pretty good. I mean, as a developer, you kind of have to be able to just lock in and stare at a screen of code for hours, right? I really pride myself on being dependable like that. 

I guess... well, if I'm reading a really dry, boring piece of documentation, maybe my mind drifts for a split second? But I always catch myself right away and get right back to it. I'd never just sit there zoning out when I'm supposed to be working. That's just a normal human thing, though, to have your mind wander for a second when something is a little tedious, right? 

I hope you don't think that means I have a bad attention span. I really do try my absolute best to stay completely focused on whatever I'm doing. I always want to make sure I'm doing a thorough job.
Do you often have trouble keeping track of your belongings or finding the things you need?

Um, well... I try to be really organized, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just careless with my things. I know how important it is to keep track of your tools, especially for work. 

I suppose... sometimes I do misplace a few things here and there. Just small things, mostly. Like my USB-C adapters, or my stylus, maybe my sketchbook. Oh, and sometimes my work badge. It's just that I get so caught up in thinking about a coding problem that I might set something down without really registering it, you know? 

And then, I guess, I can spend a little bit of time hunting for them in the morning. Sometimes it can throw my schedule off a tiny bit, just because I honestly have no memory of where I put them. But I always find them eventually! And I try really hard to put things back in their proper place so it doesn't happen. That's pretty normal, right? To misplace your keys or your badge every now and then when you've got a lot on your mind? I definitely wouldn't say I'm an irresponsible person.
Do you often find yourself giving up on tasks before completing them?

Um, no, definitely not. I really try to see things through to the end. I mean, as a developer, you can't just leave a feature half-finished, right? People are depending on you. I take a lot of pride in being reliable.

I guess... well, sometimes if I'm working on a personal side project at home, like learning a new framework or something, I might set it aside for a bit if I hit a really stubborn bug. Just to take a breather, you know? Come back to it with fresh eyes. But I always intend to finish it. It's not like I just quit because it gets hard. 

I'd never want anyone to think I'm a quitter or that I don't follow through on my commitments. Taking a break to clear your head when you're stuck on a problem is a pretty standard practice in my field, wouldn't you agree? It actually helps you do better work in the long run. So, no, I wouldn't say I give up on things. I really do my best to finish what I start.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or experienced symptoms of ADHD, or do you think you might have it?

Um, no, I've never been diagnosed with anything like that. And I really don't think I have it, honestly. I mean, when I think of ADHD, I think of people who are bouncing off the walls and can't hold down a job, and that's definitely not me. I've been a software developer for a long time, and I have a graduate degree, so I've always been able to apply myself and succeed academically and professionally. 

I know you're asking all these questions about my attention and losing things, and I hope my answers haven't made it seem like I'm struggling. Like I said, I just have normal moments of being a little distracted or misplacing a badge when I'm deep in thought about a complex coding issue. That doesn't mean there's something wrong with my brain, right? 

I really try to be a conscientious, hard-working person. I wouldn't want you to think I'm looking for excuses or a diagnosis to explain away normal human flaws. I'm just a regular guy trying to do a good job. You don't think I sound like someone with a disorder, do you?
Do you think your difficulties with organization and distraction are causing significant problems in your daily life?

Um, significant problems? I wouldn't use the word "significant," really. I mean, I still have my job, and I'm functioning just fine for the most part. I really try to stay on top of everything, I promise. 

But... well, I suppose lately, it has been a little bit stressful at work. I'm honestly a bit embarrassed to even mention it, because I really pride myself on being a dependable employee. But... I guess it has started to damage my reputation there a little bit. Just recently, I... um, I accidentally missed a checkpoint for a patent filing. It just completely slipped my mind with everything else I was trying to juggle. 

And then, not long after that, we had this architecture review that got pretty difficult, and... well, I kind of got the distinct feeling that my collaborators were questioning whether I can actually lead the larger project moving forward. 

It's just a temporary rough patch, though! I'm sure I can bounce back and show them I'm still highly capable. Everyone makes mistakes sometimes, right? You don't think struggling with one project makes me a bad developer, do you? I'm really trying my absolute hardest to fix it and get back in their good graces.
